messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: high severity — node gpu-ec2-7 is reporting repeated ephemeral storage pressure and several serve-runtime pods have been OOM/killed. Auto-eviction observed. Impact: some inference requests returning 502/timeout. Investigate and coordinate.

maria (oncall): I'm on it — pulling logs now. @kevin @julie can you both join?

kevin (eng-runtime): on my way. initial suspicion: model cache growth + logs filling /scratch. any recent deploys?

julie (sre): I see node kubelet marking ImageGC/eviction events. node reports: 
```
Kernel: Out of space on device '/dev/nvme1n1'
kubelet: eviction manager: attempting to reclaim ephemeral-storage
```

maria (oncall): kubectl get pods -n serve -o wide | grep gpu-ec2-7 shows 4 pods CrashLooping on that node. copy of describe from one pod: 
```
Events:
  Warning  Evicted  2m (x3 over 5m)  kubelet  The node was low on resource: ephemeral-storage. Container image filesystem used: 92%
  Normal   Killing   1m                 kubelet  Killing container with id docker://serve-runtime:Container failed liveness probe; OOMKilled
```

kevin (eng-runtime): can we get a snippet of serve-runtime logs? looking for CUDA errors + core dumps.

maria (oncall): grabbing logs: 
```
$ kubectl logs serve-runtime-abc -n serve -c runtime --previous
2026-03-15T14:12:03Z ERROR runtime: CUDA error: out of memory when allocating 81749632 bytes
2026-03-15T14:12:03Z ERROR runtime: could not allocate KV cache, aborting request
2026-03-15T14:12:04Z FATAL runtime: process killed: OOM
```

ricardo (support): seeing customer errors from EU region: a subset of requests retried; 5 customers reported increased latency and some 502s in last 10m. flagging for customer-ops.

sam (product-ops): what's the mitigation plan? do we have a fallback model or traffic routing to avoid impact?

kevin (eng-runtime): immediate mitigations: 1) cordon gpu-ec2-7 to stop new pods landing 2) drain the node gracefully to move live pods (kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data) 3) scale up spare capacity in Dedicated pool and shift traffic 4) restart serve-runtime after clearing /scratch/model_cache and compress logs

julie (sre): running df -h on node shows /scratch at 96% used. du suggests /scratch/model-cache and /var/log/journal are largest.

maria (oncall): executing urgent cleanup commands (will post exact commands): 
```bash
ssh admin@gpu-ec2-7
sudo systemctl stop serve-runtime
sudo du -sh /scratch/* | sort -h
sudo rm -rf /scratch/model-cache/temp_* || true
sudo journalctl --vacuum-time=2d
sudo systemctl start serve-runtime
```

maria (oncall): did the vacuum — freed ~120G, service restarted. initial pods come up but one crashed with CUDA OOM again.

kevin (eng-runtime): runtime log after restart shows model cache warmup trying to allocate full model into local cache; we need to change cache policy to on-demand to avoid big allocations on startup. pushing a quick patch to default cache policy to "lazy-load" for this cluster.

deploy-bot: Deployment 2026-03-15T14:30: patch/eng-runtime/cache-lazy-load applied to serve config (rollout in progress).

julie (sre): also increased eviction thresholds on cluster autoscaler temporarily and requested a 2-node scale up on GPU ASG.

ricardo (support): customers: error rate dropping from 7% -> 1.5% after traffic shifted to other nodes; still monitoring. updating support threads.

sam (product-ops): can we toggle a model fallback for heavy requests? fallback to redwood-lite-2B-quant for long tail heavy sequences?

kevin (eng-runtime): yes — configured routing policy to prefer fallback variant for request length > 4096 tokens and for tenants hitting >5% error. pushing policy now.

maria (oncall): handoff: kevin will take primary for the next 45 minutes to validate config + RCA primitives, julie will monitor node fleet, I will update incident channel and customer comms.

kevin (eng-runtime): current action items: 
- revert cache pre-warm in runtime and roll patch (done)
- adjust model cache size defaults for GPU instances
- add periodic cron to clear transient model temp dirs on reboot
- add alert to detect sudden /scratch growth (delta > 20% in 5m)
- follow up with infra to ensure journalctl retention not exceeding quota for GPU pool

maria (oncall): documenting impact: ~12 customers experienced degraded latency, 5 saw errors briefly. no data loss. switching to incident severity SEV2->SEV3 as customer error rate under threshold and mitigation complete.

julie (sre): node gpu-ec2-7 currently uncordoned? still cordoned. I recommend keeping cordoned until we confirm patch across images and new pods land on other nodes for 1 hour.

kevin (eng-runtime): agreed. I'll run a canary on a different node to validate the lazy-load cache behavior and monitor memory allocations.

ricardo (support): sending out customer updates: short note that we mitigated and are routing to fallback models, will follow up with postmortem.

maria (oncall): summary + post-incident tasks: 
- who owns RCA writeup? kevin (eng-runtime) to own.
- ticket for infra retention policy: julie to open.
- alert tuning: maria to add.
- customer comms: ricardo to finalize.

kevin (eng-runtime): will draft RCA and include proposed changes: default lazy cache, cap on startup prefetch, eviction-safe cleanup job, and model warmup outside node startup.

maria (oncall): handing off active oncall to kevin for next 45m, tagging done-for-now. please ack in thread when complete. :white_check_mark:

kevin (eng-runtime): ack. taking over. will post when canary validated or if anything regresses.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout complete on nodes gpu-ec2-12. All good.

maria (oncall): incident channel clear — monitoring. will create postmortem template in #postmortems and link ticket 5467.

ricardo (support): customers notified. closing customer-impact alerts but keeping internal incident open for RCA.

julie (sre): leaving note in ops runbook to monitor /scratch for GPU nodes; will add cleanup cron and retention guidelines.

maria (oncall): closing pager. thanks all.
